newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin's economic statements from TV interview.
newsitem.headline: Jospin's economic statements from TV interview.

text.p: Following are the main economic statements made by French Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin in an interview on France 2 television late on Thursday.
Public deficits:
"It's necessary to control public spending without stifling growth."
"If we have to make efforts to avoid an increase (in the deficit), these efforts must be shared fairly."
"It would be necessary to fight against deficits, even if we did not have our European commitments."
Privatisation, industrial issues:

"I think in a certain number of areas, we must look for fairly flexible methods, not to be ideological and not refuse (to accept) industrial realities in the name of non-privatisation, nor seek to privatise systematically.
"We will seek, on a case-by-case basis, the best solutions and we will explain them to the French people."

"What will guide me is industrial logic, for example in the defence industry...It will be the national interest. It will also be the cost that frequent recapitalisations in a certain number of sectors, notably banks which have experienced difficulties, involve for the state and thus for taxpayers."
"I'm not sure it's the state's role to keep on bailing out financial institutions in trouble, especially as it cannot always be done under (European Union) law..."
"And what will ultimately guide me is my attachment to public service, everything that truly concerns public service."
Single European currency:
"We want to go ahead with the single currency because it is necessary...because it is useful, notably to counter the dollar."

"...because the French want a dynamic economy, I can't take measures that will disrupt growth. At the same time...we have a commitment to go ahead with the single currency and we will do so because it is necessary."

"We will say to the French we will try and work out a way that takes into account these contradictory elements...And if we have to make a choice that goes more in one direction than in another, we will present the elements of this choice...to the country. By its response, by its indications, it will help us resolve it."

"There are other criteria (than the three percent Maastricht public deficit criterion). There's inflation -- our performance is good. There's debt -- we are below the criterion...Thus we should not speak only of this (three percent) criterion, which may suit some of our partners...It's not the only one."
Tax issues:
Asked if a decision had been taken not to go ahead with tax cuts planned by the previous conservative government, he said:
"No one has made any announcement of this type. Let us prepare the 1998 finance act which will be presented to parliament this autumn."

Will companies face new taxes? "People say 'Companies...what, you are going to tax our companies?' We are not exactly talking about companies, it could involve certain revenues which do not always come from companies."

"But in any case, for the moment, no decisions have been taken. We will make an assessment looking at how we will implement the 1997 budget we have inherited and to which we have made changes...and we have to prepare the 1998 budget. It's within this framework, in a dialogue with parliament, that decisions will be taken."
Job creation:

"If we acted now, where would we create jobs? In the (public) administration? We have said that we want to do the opposite, that we will create long-lasting jobs that will not be civil servants' jobs."

"What's important is that ministers...work on these subjects extremely closely with the majority, local authorities, associations...to prepare measures which from autumn will take into account existing realities..."
"In the second half of the year, we will put these first jobs for young people in place. But it (the ground) will have been solidly prepared."
Auto industry:
"It does not seem from what we can see that the car market in France justifies so-called Juppette or Balladurette measures."
"It seems that because these measures artificially maintained demand during these periods we had more a more brutal fall (in automobile sales)."
Family Allowances:

"To distribute family allowances on the basis of family income represents a measure of justice, especially if these decisions we are taking only affect at the end of the day a very small number of very well-off families."
